name: Sojourner
def: Six wheeled microrover of the Mars Pathfinder mission, the first wheeled vehicle to drive on another planet, operating in Ares Vallis.
body: Sojourner rolled off the Pathfinder lander on 6 July 1997 and worked in Ares Vallis, an ancient flood plain on Mars. Solar panels and non rechargeable lithium batteries powered six independently driven wheels on a rocker bogie chassis, and an alpha proton X ray spectrometer measured rock chemistry. It stayed within a few tens of metres of the lander, which relayed all of its data to Earth, and it operated for 83 sols against a planned seven.
Sojourner, named for Sojourner Truth, was the first rover on Mars, creeping a hundred metres around the Pathfinder lander in 1997 while the early web watched daily photos arrive.
facts: First wheeled robot to drive on another planet
Operated 83 sols against a planned seven sol mission
Returned 550 images and 16 rock and soil chemistry measurements
specs: Six independently driven wheels on a rocker bogie chassis
Solar array with non rechargeable lithium thionyl chloride batteries
Three cameras, laser stripe hazard detection, alpha proton X ray spectrometer
Operator designated waypoints with onboard hazard detection
